messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Wais and DIC
parts:
Hello, Aynaz.

Like you say, DIC/WAIC/CPO/CV all somehow relate to whole model predictive performance. If you are more interested in saying something about the contribution of individual covariates on the response variable, then maybe look at the change in predictive performance as variables are removed or added to a model? Maybe you could use citations below to get variable importance weights? Or maybe you just want the relative magnitude of the effects of different covariates, so you could compute standardized regression coefficients? 

Here are some citations to check out:
Gelman, A., Hwang, J. and Vehtari, A., 2014. Understanding predictive information criteria for Bayesian models. Statistics and computing, 24(6), pp.997-1016. Here: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.5928.pdf
Hooten, M.B. and Hobbs, N.T., 2015. A guide to Bayesian model selection for ecologists. Ecological monographs, 85(1), pp.3-28. Here: https://mhooten.github.io/publications/Hooten_Hobbs_EcolMono_2015.pdf
Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing. 27(5), 1413–1432. Here: doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4. Online, arXiv preprint arXiv:1507.04544.
Yao, Y., Vehtari, A., Simpson, D., and Gelman, A. (2018). Using stacking to average Bayesian predictive distributions. In Bayesian Analysis, doi:10.1214/17-BA1091. Online, arXiv preprint arXiv:1704.02030.
Gelman, A., 2008. Scaling regression inputs by dividing by two standard deviations. Statistics in medicine, 27(15), pp.2865-2873. Here: http://stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/standardizing7.pdf

Best,
Tim
